text:
julia: Heads-up: overnight we observed repeated 95th+ tail latency spikes and allocator churn on host-rack-51 (ap-south-1). A microburst from tenant W seems to trigger an IRQ cascade that knocks VF scheduling out for ~60-90s.

kevin: saw the alert. spike window 02:12-02:14 UTC. grafana link: https://grafana/redwood/d/host-egress?var-host=host-rack-51&from=now-6h

arnav: can we get the kernel irq snapshot and per-VF tx counters? wondering if MSI-X vector pool is getting exhausted.

julia: pulled quick counters and a small pcap. excerpt:
```
/proc/interrupts (snippet):
  CPU0   CPU1   CPU2   CPU3
45:  120000  430000  90000  20000  PCI-MSI  eth0-Tx-vf0
46:  10      12      8      6      PCI-MSI  eth0-Tx-vf1
47:  600000 210000  100000 50000  PCI-MSI  eth0-Rx
```
ethtool -S eth0 shows vf0 tx_packets burst to 2.1M in 30s and vf1 rx_drops spike correlated.
```

julia: pcap has a ton of small SYN/ACK bursts from tenant W during that window. They do a nightly fanout job that we thought was low-cost.

kevin: Uh. The allocator sees the host as "unhealthy" and starts warm pool fallback which causes other tenants' K/V cache hits to degrade and the edge proxy route to flip -> increased cost and 503s. Cascade.

tom: infra-bot popped: [ALERT] host-rack-51 irq-rate > 200k/s for 5m. Auto-notified oncall. :rotating_light:

infra-bot: [AUDIT] ticket INFRA-6044 created for host-rack-51 by julia (P2).

arnav: mitigation options: 1) ephemeral steer tenant W to spare-burst-pool-ap-south (higher OPEX), 2) apply per-VF egress shaping to limit microburst amplitude, 3) schedule driver+firmware upgrade to test MSI affinity fixes, 4) hard carve a dedicated VF lane (SR-IOV strict) on high-risk hosts (CAPEX/placement impact).

kevin: for immediate SLO protection I'd vote for (1) + (2) as quick windowed steps. then run lab repro for (3). (4) is a policy change for the scheduler.

julia: quick commands I'm about to run (will attach outputs):
```
# steer tenant W away for 1h
./bin/routectl steer --tenant W --to spare-burst-pool-ap-south --ttl 3600 --reason "irq-cascade protection"
# capture irq and kstat
cat /proc/interrupts > /tmp/irq_pre_move.txt
tcpdump -w /tmp/host-rack-51-burst.pcap -i eth0 -s 0 -c 50000
# add temporary per-VF throttle
tc qdisc add dev vf0 root tbf rate 200mbit burst 64k latency 100ms || true
```

carmen: +1 on steer. tagging @platform-costs: spare-burst-pool billing multiplier ~x2.2. If we keep W on spare pool permanently, ballpark OPEX delta +$9k/mo.

kevin: note for runbook: add step to check /proc/interrupts for imbalanced MSI counts and to run `irqbalance --oneshot` if imbalance found. Also capture `dmesg | grep -i flow` for driver flow-steer warnings.

arnav: lab tasks: reproduce microburst with tc/httpload, verify if NIC firmware 2.5.7 has MSI-X batching bug, test 2.5.9 candidate. Also exercise per-VF HTB shaping to find acceptable thresholds that don't hump latency.

julia: steer applied. infra-bot audit: [AUDIT] routectl steer invoked by julia for tenant W -> spare-burst-pool-ap-south TTL=3600

infra-bot: [NOTICE] auto-monitoring window set 45m. Will revert steer if stable.

tom: immediate observations: after steer + tbf, latency stabilised for other tenants, allocator churn stopped. VF drops still recorded but no cross-slice SLO impact.

carmen: Ops request: if we adopt hard VF carve policy for a subset of hosts (label: irq-harden=true) what would be the effect on bin-packing? Need scheduler team to simulate. Could increase spare capacity requirement by ~5-8% per region.

kevin: scheduler ask: add a weight to placement that penalizes multi-VF packing on irq-harden hosts. We can pilot in ap-south-1. Arnav can you PR a safe rollout?

arnav: will open PR and include a simulation job against last 3 months of allocation traces to estimate wasted slots and cost impact. Also will add a heuristic: auto-label host when /proc/interrupts shows >2x variance across MSI vectors during 5m windows.

julia: adding runbook note: "if interrupt cascade detected -> 1) steer offending tenant to spare pool 2) apply per-vf throttle 3) capture pcap/irqs 4) open driver repro 5) tag host with irq-harden? if repeating 3 times in 7 days".

kevin: final note to @platform-costs: if we choose hard carve (SR-IOV strict), CAPEX will rise non-linearly because low-util hosts increase. But steady-state OPEX may drop by reducing frequent expensive steers. Carmen will quantify.

infra-bot: [UPDATE] INFRA-6044: steer is live; monitoring shows stable SLOs at T+5m.

julia: attaching pcap + irq snapshot to ticket. will follow up with lab repro plan and a brief ops-PO meeting to decide next steps. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
